h1: Tube notchers, end formers and deburring machines
intro: A tube notcher (pipe notcher or coping machine) grinds a saddle-shaped notch into the end of a tube so it fits tightly against the tube it joins; an end former expands or reduces the tube end so two tubes slip together. The machines that finish a tube end: PN belt-sander tube notchers that cope a saddle for welded handrail, cage and frame joints at any angle to 50° with ten dovetail drums included; SFF single-station hydraulic end formers that expand or reduce tube ends to Ø3-1/2″ for exhaust slip joints and sleeves; and the TD-01 wire-brush deburring machine that cleans inside and out in one pass. They sit beside the cold saw and the tube bender and take the hand grinding out of tube fabrication — with CSA-approved panels and support from Mississauga, ON.

faq.q: What is a tube notcher for?
faq.a: When one tube meets another in a T or at an angle — handrail posts, roll cages, furniture and bike frames, trailer and gate frames — the end has to be coped to the curve of the tube it joins so the weld closes without gaps. The PN notcher grinds that saddle on a sanding belt against a drum of the mating tube's diameter in seconds, square or at any angle to 50°.

The PN 17/90 takes the larger range, 11/16″ to 3-1/2″ OD, on a 4 × 47″ belt with easy belt adjustment. The PN 20/76 is the compact notcher for 13/16″ to 3″ OD with a longer 4 × 79″ belt and a movable clamp. Both come with the same ten dovetail drums and 3 HP motor.

faq.q: Expanding or reducing — what does the end former do?
faq.a: An expander opens a tube end so the next tube slips inside (exhaust slip joints, telescoping handrail, sleeves); a reducer collapses the end to fit into the next tube. The SFF does both in one station with a hydraulic ram and interchangeable forming tools — one set is included, others are quoted to your tube size.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
